/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 12 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2852 (-65)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4148 (-192)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2432 (8)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1821 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 998 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market opened the week on a weaker note, with the BCI 182 5TC falling by $1,745 to $37,618. The Pacific was slow to get going, with just one miner in the market and limited support for rates. Offers started around $14.50 against bids at $13.00, but with little resistance, levels soon slipped below $14.00, with a couple of fixtures reported at $13.40. The C5 index fell by $0.725 to $13.510. The Atlantic was equally subdued, with sentiment remaining weak as the week got underway. Activity was limited as both owners and charterers took stock following Friday’s close. There was talk of C3 offers dipping below $33.00 towards the end of last week, although discussions remained thin today. The C3 index eased by $0.344 to $32.950. With limited fresh demand across both basins and little to suggest an immediate change in direction, the market ended the day on a softer footing, with owners facing continued downward pressure.
PANAMAX
Market sources reported a much calmer day in terms of trading activity and overall market movement within the Atlantic. The P5TC rose by $75 to $21,888, supported by a largely flat Atlantic market and some renewed momentum in the Pacific. Brokers noted an increase in trans-Atlantic demand, particularly from NC South America, although a healthy supply of available tonnage continues to temper any upward pressure. As a result, the bid-offer gap is said to have widened, with both owners and charterers testing market levels as they seek clearer direction for the week ahead. The Pacific is said to have seen a notable pickup in activity, with Indonesian demand remaining healthy. However, a substantial number of available vessels is continuing to cap any sharp upward movement in rates. Market sources have also highlighted an increase in overaged tonnage competing for Indonesian business, further intensifying competition in the region. Australia has meanwhile been described as active, helping to underpin current rate levels and drawing more modern tonnage towards longer-duration Australian trades rather than the shorter Indonesian employment options. The Yong Fa Men (74,471 2001) open in South China prompt, the Bao Neng 16 (74,492 2001) Kemen prompt, and the Shun De (70,281 1997) Ningde 20 October, were all said to have been placed on subjects for trips from Indonesia to South China at rates in the region of $15,000-$17,000. The Santa Adriana (77,040 2013) open Hong Kong 15 October was said to be on subjects for an Indonesia to Taiwan trip with Norden at $23,000, whilst the Basic Faith (82,029 2025) Zhoushan 15/17 October was fixed for an Indonesia round in the high $20,000’s, although no further details were reported.
SUPRAMAX
A typical Monday of collecting and assessing, with few reported trades emerging from Friday, as last week had ended quietly. The 11TC average managed a $94 gain to start the week at $23,023. The main driver in the index remains the North Pacific round voyage, with a reported trade at the end of last week at $25,000, but the backhaul market also appears firmer with a long trip West Africa reported at $24,000 today. Indonesia also showed improved numbers, especially for trips to India/Bangladesh and period interest continues. In the Atlantic numbers in the south softened, although sources felt this would be a small correction, whilst elsewhere the market appeared stable and fairly well balanced. The Asian Progress (64,684 2025) Tarragona 7-11 October was reported fixed for a trip via Laayoune to New Zealand intention rock phosphate at $25,000 with Damico.
HANDYSIZE
The week opened on an active but mixed footing, with the BHSI climbing by 2 points to 998 and the 7TC average gaining $44 to settle at $17,970. In the Continent and Mediterranean, the market appeared balanced, with overall demand picking up while rates held steady. The South Atlantic remained particularly strong, with rates continuing to rise. By contrast, the US Gulf remained on a softer trajectory, as demand struggled to absorb the abundant tonnage. Meanwhile, the Asian market maintained a broadly flat outlook. On the period side, the Ermione (41,240 2025) open Yangjiang 6–8 October was fixed by Norden Projects for a minimum of five to about seven months at $23,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Atlantic
The Bao Da Ling (47,426 2015) was fixed by Bulk & Metal for a trip from Izmir to the US Gulf at $10,500, although further details were not disclosed. Meanwhile, a 38,000-dwt vessel open in Marmara was fixed for a trip to the NC South America at $11,500 and another handy size heard fixed for a trip from Canakkale via CVB to Continent at $13,000 by Pangea, with limited details reported.

Asia
A 38,000-dwt vessel open in Indonesia on 16–18 October was placed on subjects for a trip to North China at $10,500, with no additional details disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Mosaic Phosphate Production Halt

Following a total of five partial curtailments and production cuts across the US and Brazil this year, Mosaic confirmed plans to temporarily halt operations at its South Fort Meade phosphate mine in Florida, citing problems with sulphur availability and affordability, CRU reports. This is the second largest of Mosaic’s three US mines, with an annual nameplate capacity of 5.5 Mtpa, and phosphate rock output estimated at 2.2 Mtpa in 2026 per CRU.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape

Cape was weaker overall, with heavy activity across the front months and Q1 as prices moved lower. Oct opened around 35,500, with heavy volume around 35,250 late. Nov traded up to 38,750 early before weakening to 38,000 and later 37,650–37,850. Dec opened around 39,000 before easing to 38,450–38,700. Q4 26 fell from 37,600 to 37,000 before recovering towards 37,350. Q1 27 softened from 29,000 to 28,450–28,600, while Q2 27 eased from 35,000 to around 34,600–34,750. Cal 27 weakened from 32,550 to 32,150, with significant volume at the lower levels. Cal 28 printed at 27,500.
